svg.text: The narrowed goal lint — what it still refuses, and what it lets through
A refusal names a defect in the brief: an unresolved placeholder, or a goal that really is two deliverables.
1. An unresolved placeholder?
an angle-bracket token such as <node> sits in the
goal or the done-when — but a quoted string or a
code span is the author quoting a literal, so its
contents are data to reproduce, not a gap to fill
refused as: fully-specified
2. A vague word in the goal?
TBD, TODO, FIXME, ???, "figure out", "somehow",
or "as appropriate" standing in for the work — a
goal that is nothing but one such word is refused,
while a done-when may name a marker to count
refused as: fully-specified
3. Two deliverables in one goal?
a separator — ; "then" "and" "&" "plus" — opens a
second deliverable only when the clause after it
begins with its own action verb. One verb over
several objects stays one node
refused as: single-goal
Accepted — the work stands
a semicolon or "then" joining one deliverable;
one verb over several objects;
a done-when quoting a <path> runtime message;
a done-when counting TODO-FIXME, xfail, skip
all eight properties still judged; only these two speak to the goal
Refused — with the property named
fully-specified for a placeholder or vague goal;
single-goal for two verb-object clauses;
and, when the caller passes the role's fit,
fully-specified for a measure the role cannot run
the detail says which input to state, not just that it failed
no
no
yes
